Jugendra Singh R/o Village Puraini Deep Nagar, Po Mahna Japti, Ps Madhotanda, Distt. Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh ....Driver-cum-owner /respondent no.1 2. New India Assurance Company Ltd. Bajaj House, 97, Nehru Place, New Delhi-110019. ....Insurance/respondent no.2 Date of accident : 28.11.2017 Result of accident : Grievous injury Date of filing of Petition : 28.09.2018 Date of Decision : 29.04.2025 Mact No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 1 of 21 ss Digitall signed b Charu Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.04. 16:10:09 +0530 Award Ambrish Kumar vs Shital Singh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182445951/ 1 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Ambrish Kumar Singh, aged about 58 years, suffered grievous injury.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Ambrish Kumar Singh, aged about 58 years, suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 28.11.2017 at about 10:30 PM, Sh. Ambrish Kumar Singh along with his wife (since deceased) were travelling from Gram Madhotanda to Puranpur on a motorcycle bearing no. DL-26F-7259. When they reached near Gulabtanda Mod a motorcycle bearing no. UP-26P-7377 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) coming to Madhotanda, at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle of the petitioner. As an impact of the collision, petitioner and his wife fell on the road. While petitioner sustained grievous injury, his wife Smt. Suman Singh lost her life in the accident. 3. An FIR No.0733/17 dated 28.11.2017 u/s 279/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Madhotanda, District Pilibhit. Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and two separate claim petitions were filed by the petitioner in respect of injury sustained by him and qua death of his wife before this Tribunal. The connected claim petition qua death of Smt. Suman Singh is MACT No. 914/18. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven and owned by respondent no.1 and insured with respondent no. 2. In response to the claim, respondent no.1 filed his reply denying the occurrence of the accident and refuting the allegations of rash and negligent driving on the part of driver-cum-owner. It is MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 2 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.29 16:10:14 +0530 pleaded that the respondent was having a valid driving licence and his vehicle was duly insured. 5. Respondent no. 2/insurance company filed its reply/written statement denying its liability to compensate the petitioners on the ground that the petitioner was himself in breach traffic rules as his vehicle was uninsured. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 27.03.2019. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 28.11.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-26P-7377 driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2 ? OPP. 7. Thereafter, evidence was led by the petitioner by examining himself as PW-1 and Ms. Bhagwati Singh as PW-2. PW-1 / petitioner Ambrish Kumar tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated that the accident occurred on 28.11.2017 at about 10:30 a.m. when he was going on his motorcycle No.UP-26F-7259 to Puranpur from Madhotanda and when they reached near the turn of Gulabtanda, a motorcycle no.UP-26P-7377 which was coming from opposite direction in a drastic speed as well as in a very rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the victim. Due to which injured sustained injuries. PW-1 further deposed that he was working as a Manager with Bhagwati Farms, Village & PO Madhotanda, tehsel Kali Nagar, Distt Pilibhit and was earning of MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 3 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.29 16:10:27 +0530 Rs.20,000/- per month. He relied upon his Adhar Card & PAN card as Ex.PW1/1, his driving licence as Ex.PW1/2, Educational documents as Ex.PW1/3, medical prescription as Ex.PW1/4, Medical bills as Ex.PW1/5, FIR as Ex.PW1/6, site plan Ex.PW1/7, chargesheet as Ex.PW1/8, driving licence of driver of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/9, RC of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/10 and insurance policy of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/11. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for driver cum owner and counsel for insurance company. PW-2 /Bhagwati Singh tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW2/A wherein he deposed that he is co-owner of Agricultural land in Village & PO Madhotanda, Tehsil Kali Nagar, Distt. Pilibhit under the name of Bhagwati Farms having approx area of 22 acres and involved in growing agricultural crops. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.PW2/1 and computer generated record pertaining to the agricultural land as Ex.PW2/2. PW-2 was not cross-examined by respondents despite opportunity. It is argued on behalf of the claimants that the accident was caused by respondent no.1 by driving the offending motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner. He has categorically deposed that the accident was a head on collision with the offending vehicle which suddenly came from the wrong side of MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 5 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Despite cross examining PW-1, no suggestion denying the occurrence of the accident or negligence on the part of respondent no.1 has been put by the insurance company. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.
texts.arguments: It is argued that since respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle, which is owned by him and insured with respondent no. 2, both the respondents are liable to compensate the petitioner. On the other hand, it is the argument of respondent no. 2 that the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured cannot be fastened with liability to compensate the petitioners as neither negligence of respondent no.1 is proved nor the occurrence of the accident. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 13. The driver of the offending vehicle has not entered the witness box or raised any defence to negate or refute the allegations of rash and negligent driving. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In the present case also, driver did not enter into the witness box to controvert the Ambrish Kumar vs Shital Singh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182445951/ 4 claim of petitioner or even to explain circumstances of accident. 14. Further, even MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 6 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.29 16:10:40 +0530 the medical documents and the contents of the chargesheet, support the claimant that injuries were caused in road the accident due to negligence of respondent no.1. 17. Further it is noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 7 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.29 16:10:45 +0530 (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 17.1 17.2 It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 17.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 8 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.29 16:11:55 +0530 evidence. 17.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 16 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.29 16:12:33 +0530 formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. Apportionment:- 27. 28. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Ambrish Kumar vs Shital Singh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182445951/ 11 In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 17 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.29 16:12:37 +0530 the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. The MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 18 of 21 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.04.29 16:12:41 +0530 guidelines were not to be understood to mean that the Tribunals were to take a rigid stand while considering an application seeking release of the money. However, it is seen that even in cases when there is no possibility or chance of the feed being frittered away by the beneficiary owing to ignorance, illiteracy or susceptibility to exploitation, investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit is directed by the Tribunals as a matter of course and in a routine manner, ignoring the object and the spirit of the Ambrish Kumar vs Shital Singh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182445951/ 12 guidelines issued by this Court and the genuine requirements of the claimants. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him. MACT No.915/18 Ambrish vs.Shital Singh & anr. P.No. 19 of 21 ss CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.04.29 16:12:46 +0530 29.
